cases.answer: Gao's nomogram does not report a ten-year risk. It predicts MACE over 1-year follow-up. It was derived in 131 patients and externally validated in 288 patients. The external cohort had a 31.6% 1-year MACE rate, against 16.4% in the derivation cohort. The external validation AUC was 0.932. The authors say longer follow-up and harder endpoints are needed.

cases.answer: Gao's CCTA nomogram combines eight CCTA parameters to predict 1-year MACE in CAD patients. Its combined model reached AUC 0.936 (apparent, derivation; optimism-corrected C-index 0.917) and 0.932 in the external cohort. Sun's no-reflow study found the CHA2DS2-VA score alone gave AUC 0.613 overall. Adding sex, hemoglobin, platelets, lymphocytes and stent number (Model 2) gave 0.689 overall. In males the score alone gave 0.569 and the combined model 0.721 (vs 0.682 in females). The tasks differ in outcome, population and timing. Gao predicts later clinical events (mostly rehospitalization for unstable angina) over 1 year in CAD patients, using post-hoc imaging. Sun predicts an acute angiographic complication, no-reflow, during primary PCI in STEMI patients, using clinical score plus lab and procedural variables.

cases.answer: In the Inverse T2D-BP risk cluster (353 SNVs), alleles that raise T2D risk are associated with lower SBP/DBP/PP. Aligned to the T2D risk allele, they are also associated with lower risk of AF, CAD, stroke and heart failure. They show associations with higher BMI and higher insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). The cluster's partitioned PGS is protective against hypertension (OR 0.91) and CAD (OR 0.94), which is the opposite pattern to the Metabolic Syndrome cluster. It should not be read as a drug-response result because the evidence is genetic variant association and polygenic-score analysis in a cohort, not treatment or pharmacological data. The authors only say the findings 'support previous research' on heterogeneous effects of hypertensive medications. They offer a retinol-metabolism hypothesis and note the pattern may instead reflect incomplete overlap in the genetic architectures of T2D and BP. The paper does not itself state a drug-response caveat, so this reasoning is an inference.
